what: Refusals tsfga makes that OpenFGA does not. Each is a divergence, not a parity claim, and it is here rather than in `write-gate-causes.json` because it has no upstream cause to biject to -- upstream accepts the input.

Two lists rather than one list with an exception. An escape hatch inside the bijection would let any future rule opt out of the completeness argument by declaring itself special; a second list cannot, because it is a public inventory of places tsfga knowingly differs.

A rule cannot declare itself a capability refusal. Every entry names a conformance test that uses a pin helper, and the pin helpers refuse to pass on agreement -- so an entry must exhibit a case where OpenFGA demonstrably accepts what tsfga refuses. The day upstream starts refusing it too, the pin fails and the entry moves to the upstream list.

refusals.reason: cel-go's `matches` is RE2 and cel-js's is a JavaScript `RegExp`. They disagree on which patterns are legal, on what several constructs mean, and on whether a pattern terminates at all; a write-time gate over literal patterns closed one of those three groups and none of the others. So the call is not declared, and a condition using it is refused at the model write.
